root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Martian Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Bf5 5. Ng5 Bg6 6. N1f3 h6 7. Ne6

overview: In the Classical Caro-Kann White sacrifices a knight on e6 against the queen, hoping for an attack on f7 and a lead in development after ...fxe6 or ...Qd7. Black can simply take the piece and, with accurate play, keep it, since White's pieces are not placed to exploit the opened f-file. It is a trap line that scores through surprise.

white_ideas.idea: Sacrifice on e6 and open the f-file for Bd3 and Qe2
Trade pieces and use the weakened pawn structure after ...fxe6

black_ideas.idea: Capture the knight and give back material only for safety
Develop with ...Nf6, ...e6 and consolidate, then convert the extra piece

typical_structures.structure: Black with an extra piece and a damaged pawn structure on e6/f7, White ahead in development

character.notes: White sacrifices a piece for an attack; one side collapses quickly.

gambit.notes: After 7...fxe6 White has given a knight for a pawn and Black can keep the extra material.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound; the sacrifice does not produce enough compensation against accurate defence.

structure.notes: Open d-file and f-file after the exchanges.

approach.notes: Played mainly as a surprise; strong players rarely choose it.

level.notes: A trap that depends on prepared lines.

sublines_that_differ.name: Classical main line
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Bf5 5. Ng3 Bg6

character.reason: A piece sacrifice for an attack is forcing and risky for both sides.

gambit.reason: White gives a knight for a pawn on e6 and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Strong players think the sacrifice insufficient.

structure.reason: The d- and f-files open and pieces play on open lines.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom play the Martian Gambit.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner and it is trap-led rather than deep.

plans.reason: White's compensation is speed of development and pressure on f7.
